USER PREFERENCE: The user requested to ALSO generate Batch Client Extensions (Liferay Objects) for any backend entities used/referenced by this module (e.g. Book, Author). Generate the Object Definition batch files and client-extension.yaml so that the Custom Element has an active backend API (/o/c/[slug]).

Determine:
1. Liferay Object definitions (ignoring audit fields like companyId, userId, createDate), ONLY if backend objects are requested.
2. Required Batch Client Extension structure, ONLY if backend objects are requested.
3. Frontend UI components (React JavaScript Custom Elements or Page Fragments), if portlets exist.
4. Model Listeners / Service Wrappers mapping (Native Object Actions vs Object Action CETs).
5. API CONTRACT (ALWAYS include it, even if backend objects are not generated): a section titled '## API CONTRACT' listing,
   for each Liferay Object: its name (PascalCase, e.g. DevconRegistration), its externalReferenceCode, and its REST endpoint
   '/o/c/' + the lowercase plural of the name with only letters and digits (e.g. '/o/c/devconregistrations');
   for each Picklist: its externalReferenceCode and its entries URL
   '/o/headless-admin-list-type/v1.0/list-type-definitions/by-external-reference-code/[ERC]/list-type-entries'.
   The backend and frontend coders work in parallel and never see each other's files: this contract is the ONLY way they agree on names, codes and URLs.

--- File: service.xml ---
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE service-builder PUBLIC "-//Liferay//DTD Service Builder 7.3.0//EN" "http://www.liferay.com/dtd/liferay-service-builder_7_3_0.dtd">

<service-builder dependency-injector="ds" package-path="com.acme.library">
	<namespace>Library</namespace>
	<entity local-service="true" name="Book" remote-service="true" uuid="true">
		<column name="bookId" primary="true" type="long" />
		<column name="companyId" type="long" />
		<column name="title" type="String" />
		<column name="format" type="String" />
		<column name="status" type="int" />
	</entity>
	<entity local-service="true" name="Author" remote-service="false">
		<column name="authorId" primary="true" type="long" />
		<column name="name" type="String" />
	</entity>
</service-builder>


--- File: java:scheduler:OverdueBooksScheduler.java ---
package com.acme.library.scheduler;

import com.acme.library.model.Book;
import com.liferay.mail.kernel.model.MailMessage;
import com.liferay.mail.kernel.service.MailServiceUtil;
import com.liferay.portal.kernel.messaging.BaseMessageListener;
import com.liferay.portal.kernel.messaging.Message;

import javax.mail.internet.InternetAddress;

public class OverdueBooksScheduler extends BaseMessageListener {

	@Override
	protected void doReceive(Message message) throws Exception {
		MailMessage mailMessage = new MailMessage(
			new InternetAddress("library@acme.com"),
			new InternetAddress("member@acme.com"), "Overdue", "Return it", false);

		MailServiceUtil.sendEmail(mailMessage);
	}

}


--- File: java:listener:BookModelListener.java ---
package com.acme.library.model.listener;

import com.acme.library.model.Book;
import com.acme.library.model.BookModel;
import com.liferay.portal.kernel.model.BaseModelListener;
import com.liferay.portal.kernel.model.ModelListener;

import org.osgi.service.component.annotations.Component;

@Component(service = ModelListener.class)
public class BookModelListener extends BaseModelListener<Book> {

	@Override
	public void onAfterCreate(Book book) {
		System.out.println("Created book " + book.getTitle());
	}

}

import javax.mail.internet.InternetAddress;

public class OverdueBooksScheduler extends BaseMessageListener {

	@Override
	protected void doReceive(Message message) throws Exception {
		MailMessage mailMessage = new MailMessage(
			new InternetAddress("library@acme.com"),
			new InternetAddress("member@acme.com"), "Overdue", "Return it", false);

		MailServiceUtil.sendEmail(mailMessage);
	}

}
